paragraphs.text: Updates and plugin management UI for the DeepSeek Harness Windows desktop app: a sidebar entry, a pa
nel and a Settings section, driven by the app's native bridge.
# dsh-plugin-desktop-updates
**A DeepSeek Harness plugin that renders the Updates UI of the Windows desktop app: a row beside Set
tings, an Updates panel, and an Updates section, driven by the app's native page bridge.**
It shows the desktop app's version, the installed and published harness versions, and the plugins th

is home
runs — with the actions to check, download, install, restart, repair the harness, and enable

, disable, install
or remove plugins.
> **Project status:** 1.3.0, published on npm. Verified against the DeepSeek Harness **0.1.5-rc.x**

runtime
> that the Windows desktop app bundles. **The desktop app it serves is archived**, and this

plugin depends on
> that app's own page bridge (`window.__dshDesktop`), which the official DeepSeek

Harness desktop app does not
> provide. In the official app the plugin loads and renders, but report

s that the bridge is unavailable —
> because it is. See §Why this exists.
## Screenshots
The UI appears in the desktop app that bundles it. Screenshots of the app window, including the Upda

tes panel,
are in
the app repository.
## Why this exists
The app needed a settings surface — the app's version, whether the harness was current, what plugins

this home
runs, and buttons to act on all of it — without rebuilding a native window for every chan

ge. The app already
rendered the harness web UI in WebView2, so the surface became a plugin: sidebar

row, panel and Settings
section, all in the page the user is already looking at.
That decision had one consequence worth stating. The facts and the actions live in the **app**, not

the page,
so the page needs a channel back to it. The app injects a versioned bridge, `window.__dshD

esktop`, into every
page it loads, and this plugin is the only consumer of it.
**That bridge is the reason this plugin is tied to one app.** The official DeepSeek Harness desktop

app ships
its own plugin manager and its own updates view; it does not expose `__dshDesktop`. Instal

led there, this plugin
registers its slots and then reports that it cannot reach the app — which is

accurate, and better than a panel
that looks live and does nothing.
## What it does
- **A row beside Settings** in the sidebar — a labelled entry (an icon in the 56 px rail) that opens

the Updates
panel, with a dot when a newer app build exists.
- **A panel**, full view, in the app's

own window: the facts plus check, download, install, restart and
repair, and the plugin list with e

nable, disable, install and remove.
- **A Settings section** with the same facts and actions in a na

rrower form.
- **Reports what the shell refused.** The shell drops a slot registration it dislikes w

ithout telling anyone, so
a plugin whose UI never appears looks exactly like one that never loaded.

This plugin publishes what it
registered — and every refusal — to `window.__dshDesktopUpdates` and t

o the app's log.
- **Degrades honestly.** With no bridge, it says the app is unavailable instead of
pretending the panel works.
## How it works
### The four slots it contributes
| Slot | Entry | What it renders |
| `sidebar.footer.action` | id `desktop-updates` | A labelled row beside Settings (an icon in the 56

px rail) that opens the Updates panel; a dot when a newer app build exists |
| `sidebar.panellist`
| id `desktop-updates` | The sidebar row for the Updates panel, addressed by the same id as the body

below |
| `main` | key `desktop-updates` | The Updates panel itself: the full view, in the app's ow

n window |
| `settings.section` | id `desktop-updates` | The concise view inside Settings, with the
same facts and actions |
The three list slots require an `id` and the keyed `main` slot requires a `key`; the shell rejects a
registration that omits either.
### Opening the panel is a layout action, not a bridge call
The plugin selects its own panel through `ctx.layout.selectPanel`, so the view appears in the window

the user
is already looking at, and opening it cannot fail because the bridge is unavailable. When

the shell has no
panel slot to select, it falls back to the app's native updates window — the same w
indow the tray menu opens.
### The registration marker
`client.js` writes `window.__dshDesktopUpdates` as it applies: the slots it registered and every con

tribution
the shell refused. The app reads that marker after each page load and logs it. The Updates

section repeats any
refusal, because that is the only place a user would see it.
### Version skew
The app leaves an installed version alone when it is newer than the copy inside its executable, so a

newer npm
release is not undone by the next launch. `DeepSeekHarness.exe --install-plugin` restores

the bundled copy
deliberately.
## Requirements
- A DeepSeek Harness **0.1.x** composition with the `layout` service — the runtime the Windows deskt

op app
bundles.
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout`, declared in `dsh.client.inject`, which the ho

st must provide.
- For anything to be actionable: the desktop app's `window.__dshDesktop` bridge.
## Quick start
### Install from npm
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Install into the desktop app
The app installs its bundled copy by itself, into the harness home it owns. From inside the app, use
**Settings → Updates → the plugin manager**, which accepts a package name, a git spec or a local fo

lder.
Installing from npm replaces the bundled copy with the published one.
### Build from source
Nothing to build — the client half is a hand-written module-face bundle:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Security
This plugin is a **UI that asks the app to act**. It performs no update, install or removal itself:

every
button posts a message over the app's bridge, and the app does the work with its own verificat

ion — checksum
verification of downloads, and the harness's own plugin manager for installs.
It makes no network calls, reads no credentials, and writes no files. It does read app and harness v

ersion
state through the bridge, which is not sensitive.
Installing *any* plugin runs host code outside the workspace sandbox; that is a property of the harn

ess, not of
this plugin. Install from the npm package or from source you have read.
Report a vulnerability through the process in SECURITY.md.
